alt: Five areas of life chances: health and life expectancy, education, employment and income, housing, and treatment by the criminal justice system. Below, two schematic groups of twenty dots: more members of one group reach a good outcome, but some members of the other group still do.
caption: Life chances are about probabilities across several areas, not certainties.

after: ## A grid for explaining any factor
alt: A chain from factor to mechanism to outcome: social class works through low income, damp housing and a poor diet to raise the risk of illness. Below, four more chains: gender through unpaid caring and the glass ceiling, age through ageism, disability through barriers and attitudes, and sexuality through prejudice and bullying.
caption: Name the factor, give the mechanism, then the outcome it affects.

after: ## A grid for explaining any factor
alt: Left: the Equality Act 2010 protects against discrimination on grounds including age, disability, race, religion or belief, sex and sexual orientation. Right: its limits: discrimination is hard to prove, unpaid caring is not covered, and prejudice has not disappeared.
caption: The law offers protection, but it cannot remove every inequality in life chances.

alt: Functionalists see differences in life chances as fair outcomes of talent and effort, with social mobility. Against them, Marxists and feminists both see structured inequality but disagree on the main cause: class and capitalism for Marxists, patriarchy for feminists.
caption: Functionalists see fair outcomes; Marxists and feminists see structured inequality, but disagree on its cause.
